input.brief: Bellis Australia: industrial mechanical insulation distributor, metal fabricator and installer serving LNG, power, mining, marine and defence plants

direction.name: The specimen catalogue
direction.idea: Present what is on offer the way a field guide presents birds: each item alone on a flat colour, same scale, same angle, named plainly. A bakery's pastries become specimens and the specimens become the menu. A furniture maker's chairs each get their own colour tile. The format flatters ordinary objects because it treats each as worth looking at, and it replaces both the feature grid and the product-card grid with something that has a point of view.
direction.composition: Hero: a left-aligned statement of what this is (5–7vw, upper-left) beside or above a tight cluster of four to seven specimen tiles of different sizes arranged as a loose mosaic that runs off the right edge. Each tile is a flat colour square or 4:5 rectangle with one photograph centred on it, no border, 8–12px gaps. The main section is the catalogue itself: a grid of tiles in which each item has its name and one fact set beneath the tile in the text face, aligned left to the tile edge. Tile colours rotate through three or four fields from the palette. One tile in every six or seven is double size. Supporting sections (about, how to order) are plain text on the ground colour, kept short.
direction.typography: Friendly and plain. Item names at 18–22px in medium weight, facts beneath in the soft ink. One big statement in the hero; no other display type.
direction.colour: The tiles are the colour: three or four flat fields from the palette, repeated in a steady rotation. Ground stays neutral.
direction.imagery: Photographs of single items on plain backgrounds, all cropped to sit at the same apparent size within their tile. On light tiles, `mix-blend-mode: multiply` removes white studio backgrounds. If the subject's own item photographs are missing, use the dealt set and say so.
direction.richness: Rhythm of colour tiles and the pleasure of comparing like with like.
direction.pitfalls: It needs at least six items that can be shown as objects; with three it is a feature row. Keep labels outside the tiles. No shadows under the objects, no hover lift.

hero.name: Anchored text, specimen half
hero.blueprint: The viewport is split exactly in half by two flat tones that meet at a clean vertical edge: the ground on the left, a palette colour on the right. Left half: the wordmark sits top-left on a 40px margin; the next two thirds of the height are empty; everything else is anchored bottom-left and ends 40px above the bottom edge: a headline on one or two lines at clamp(28px, 2.6vw, 40px), medium weight; one sentence at 18px in the soft ink, max 38ch; the single action as a solid rectangle. Right half: position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh. In its centre sits a square tile in a second palette colour, 450px wide (31vw) with a 24px radius, holding one cut-out item at 70% of the tile, object-fit: contain, mix-blend-mode: multiply on light fills. Under the tile's left corner the item's name and one fact sit at 15px. As the left column scrolls through the catalogue, the tile's item and colour swap to match the entry in view. One text link sits top-right on the colour field.
hero.mobile: The colour half comes first as a block 52svh tall holding the square tile at 62vw, centred, and stays sticky while the text slides over its lower edge. The text block follows on the ground: the headline at 7vw on two lines, the sentence at 16px, the action full width. The wordmark and one link sit on the top row over the colour.
hero.headline: A modest 3-6 word line at 28-40px, at most 40 characters; the object, not the type, carries the screen.

type.note: A soft geometric sans with wide round letters and relaxed joins, warm at semibold and easy at text size. Suits consumer apps, community products, cafes and small friendly brands.

palette.name: Card pastels
palette.note: Neutral paper ground and black type, with each card or tile given its own flat pastel (periwinkle, lime, amber or cyan), never two alike side by side. Magenta is reserved for the logo, the email address and text links.

motion.name: Pinned story
motion.description: One element holds its place with `position: sticky` (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it. The page's ordinary scrolling does the work; nothing is hijacked. Hold it for about one screen per step and three screens at most, two held stages per page at most, with a line of text on every held screen. Recipe: 'Pinned story' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Four cards dealt into a fan
sections.blueprint: Four values, rules or features, each on a card dealt onto the table as the page scrolls. A wrapper about 400svh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh on the page's darkest flat ground. Each card is a portrait panel of 340×400px with a 20px radius, filled with its own palette colour (four colours that differ clearly in lightness), no border, no shadow. On a card, with 28px padding: its name at 32px in heavy capitals on one or two lines at the top, a photograph or a single picture of the thing at 60% of the card's width in the middle, and one sentence at 16px at the foot. Card one lands alone at the centre; each further quarter of the wrapper deals the next from below the bottom edge, landing 250px to the right of the one before, rotated between -4 and 4 degrees and overlapping only its right 90px, until the four form a fan about 1,090px wide centred on the stage. Keep each card's name, picture and sentence inside its left 240px, so no card ever covers another's words. In the study the cards overlap by two thirds and bury the earlier titles; here nothing lies on top of text. The heading, two to four words at clamp(40px, 4vw, 60px), sits top-left on the stage on the 32px margin with one sentence at 17px under it. The stage releases after the fourth card has settled; under reduced motion the fan is simply there.
sections.mobile: No pin. The cards sit in one row that scrolls sideways with scroll-snap, each 82% of the width with the next peeking in at the right edge, all upright. The heading and sentence sit above the row.

sections.name: Object on a disc
sections.blueprint: One section about a viewport tall on a plain ground. A flat filled disc 64vh across, in one palette colour, sits with its centre at 58% of the width; swap the disc for the subject's own shape if it has one. A cut-out object photograph stands in front of it, centred on it, about 78% of the disc's height and breaking the disc's outline at the top. Bottom-left, starting on the margin and ending level with the disc's lower edge: a vertical list of four to six item names at clamp(28px, 2.9vw, 44px), leading 1.15. The selected name is in full ink and the rest at 25%; choosing a name swaps the object (300ms crossfade) and the disc's colour. The heading, two to four words at the same size as the names but in the soft ink, is the first line of that list. One fact about the selected item sits at the disc's right edge at 17px.
sections.mobile: The disc comes first, 86vw across and centred, with the object in front. The names follow as a single sideways-scrolling line at 26px with 24px gaps, the selected one in full ink. The fact sits under the names at 16px.

sections.name: Tiles that grow
sections.blueprint: Order is carried by size. Three flat colour tiles stand in one row, bottom-aligned (align-items: end) with 10px gaps, each larger than the one before: columns 1–3 at 30vh tall, columns 4–7 at 44vh, columns 8–12 at 60vh. Each tile holds one photograph of the subject at that stage (raw, in progress, finished), centred and scaled so the object grows from tile to tile; on light tiles mix-blend-mode: multiply removes a white studio background. One palette colour per tile. Text sits under the tiles, outside them, aligned to each tile's left edge: a stage name at 20px medium whose wording carries the order ('Picked', 'Pressed', 'Poured') and two lines at 16px in the soft ink. The heading, two to four words at 40–52px, occupies the empty ground above the two smaller tiles, top-aligned with the tallest tile. A fourth stage is possible with spans of 2, 3, 3 and 4 columns.
sections.mobile: Tiles stack in order and grow in height instead: 34vw, 46vw and 62vw tall, each at full width. The name and text sit under each tile at 18px and 16px. The heading comes first at 30px. 28px between stages.

sections.name: The printed guest list
sections.blueprint: Names are printed on a card, the way a programme lists its patrons or an invitation its hosts. On a contrasting flat ground, a paper-coloured panel about 56% of the viewport wide with 5:7 proportions sits centred and rotated by one or two degrees; the section is shorter than the card and clips it with `overflow: hidden`, so the card is cut by the bottom edge rather than framed whole. Inside, 56px padding. At the top, a centred heading of two to four words at 28px. Below it the names run as centred lines at 20–22px with leading 1.7, several names to a line, separated by middots with a non-breaking space either side. One photograph may be tipped in between the heading and the names: 16:9, the full inner width, square corners. The card is a plain filled shape with no outline.
sections.mobile: The card becomes 92% of the screen wide, keeps a one-degree tilt and is still cut off by the section's bottom edge. Heading at 22px, names at 17px with two names to a line. Padding drops to 28px, and the tipped-in photograph keeps the full inner width.

sections.name: Stepped figure tiles
sections.blueprint: Three figures on three tiles that refuse to line up. A tall tile in the accent colour fills columns 1–6 and is 70vh high; it holds one figure at clamp(56px, 5.4vw, 92px) in its top-left corner, 28px in, and its caption at 17px in its bottom-left corner, with empty colour between. On the right, an ink-coloured tile in columns 7–9 starts 14vh lower and is 44vh high: a paper-coloured figure top-left, a caption along its bottom edge. A third tile in a mid tone takes columns 10–12, starts 26vh down and is 34vh high, with the same internal layout. Gaps are 8px. The unequal heights leave notches of bare ground above and below the right-hand tiles; the heading, two to four words at 28–36px, sits in the upper notch on column 7. If the page has a motif, cut one corner of each tile to its geometry with clip-path.
sections.mobile: The tall tile comes first, at full width and 56vw high, with its figure at 15vw. The two smaller tiles follow side by side with a 6px gap, the right one starting 32px lower than the left, each with its figure at 11vw and its caption at the bottom. The heading sits above at 26px.

sections.name: Object riding down the schedule
sections.blueprint: A schedule of dated events (races, concerts, tastings, departures) with the subject's own object travelling down it. On a dark flat ground, on the page's own margins, the heading is one centred line of condensed capitals at clamp(40px, 3.6vw, 56px), split into its two words with a gap between them, and in the gap stands a cut-out photograph of the object seen from above or in profile, about 320px wide (22% of the width) and up to 64% of the viewport tall. Below come full-width rows 84px tall, each a two-part grid: the event's name at 26px in condensed capitals on the left with a one-line note at 16px in the soft ink under it, and the date and place right-aligned at 16px on the note's baseline. Rows alternate between the ground and a tone one step lighter instead of rules. As the page scrolls, the object leaves the heading and moves down the centre line over the rows (`position: sticky` in a centred column that spans the list, `pointer-events: none`), where it covers only the empty middle of each row and marks how far the reader has come. The row for the next event takes the accent colour across its whole band, with its name and date in the accent's ink. About ten rows fit on one screen; the list ends 120px under the last row.
sections.mobile: Rows stack at full width on 20px margins: the name at 22px on up to two lines, the note at 16px, the date under the note. The object shrinks to 40% of the width and stays in the heading; it does not travel, because on a phone it would cover the rows. The accent band stays on the next event.

sections.name: Photo strip, three-cell bar
sections.blueprint: A saturated flat field about 80svh tall. Across the top, 48px from the section edge, a strip of small photographs runs off both sides: all 150px tall at differing widths (3:4, 1:1, 3:2 in turn), 8px gaps, ten or more, drifting slowly as a marquee. A heading of two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px) sits 72px below the strip at the left margin. 40px below the heading, the newsletter or booking form is one bar spanning the content width, 96px tall, divided into three equal cells with 8px gaps. Each cell is a filled block in a tone one step from the field with one radius: the first two are inputs (name, email) with placeholder text centred at 18px, the third is the submit action in the inverse colours with its word centred. Focus changes a cell's fill to the lightest tone. Small print at 13px sits under the first and third cells.
sections.mobile: The strip is 110px tall and scrolls by touch. The heading follows at 9vw. The three cells stack as full-width filled blocks 60px tall with 8px gaps, the submit block last. Small print sits beneath the stack, left-aligned.

sections.name: The action tile
sections.blueprint: The close is one row of the board. Three filled tiles sit side by side with 8–14px gaps, all 360px tall and sharing one radius: a wide centre tile spanning columns 3–10 in the accent colour, flanked by two narrow tiles (columns 1–2 and 11–12) that run off the left and right viewport edges, as if the row had been cropped from a longer one. The centre tile holds, left-aligned and vertically centred with 40px padding: a heading of three to five words at 40px, two lines at 17px, and the action. The action is either one rectangular button or an email field 420px wide in the paper colour with the submit button nested inside its right end. The flanking tiles hold no text: one is a photograph covering the tile, the other a flat palette colour. No shadows, no outlines.
sections.mobile: The accent tile runs full width, about 300px tall, heading at 28px, field and button stacked at full width. The two flanking tiles follow beneath as a pair, each half width and 120px tall, with the same gap and the same radius.

sections.name: The back of the card
sections.blueprint: The footer is the reverse side of the page's artefact, laid out as the back of a postcard. A paper-coloured panel spans columns 2–11 on the contrasting ground, about 420px tall, its top edge cut into a row of twelve semicircular scallops (an inline SVG path or `clip-path`, each scallop about 100px wide). The panel is divided by space into two halves. Left half: a short sign-off of two to four words at 32px, then two or three lines at 16px, written like a message. Right half: the address block, four left-aligned lines at 18px with 12px between them, each line a link (email, telephone, street, social); above it in the top-right corner, a stamp: one small photograph, 3:4 and 88px wide, with a 6px paper-coloured margin. Along the panel's bottom edge, a single centred line at 12px gives the copyright like a printer's imprint.
sections.mobile: The panel runs full width with six scallops across its top edge. The stamp sits top-right at 64px wide; the sign-off and message come first, then the address lines at 17px beneath them, then the imprint line centred at 12px.

references.name: Noho
references.idea: Furniture sold through people misusing it (wearing, balancing on, hiding behind chairs on flat colour backdrops) while the interface stays quiet beige.
references.hero: The viewport splits exactly 50/50 by tone alone: left half warm off-white, right half a slightly darker greige, no rule. Left: a small lowercase logo top-left at 30px margin, then a four-line bold headline at 60px (4.2vw), tracking -0.04em and leading near 1.0, top-left aligned and filling the upper 40%; the lower half is empty except for a one-line 18px tagline pinned bottom-left. Right: a staggered mosaic of seven portrait photos, each about 175 by 230px with 15px gaps, on a four-column, three-row grid with several cells left empty and the rightmost image cropped by the viewport edge. A white square menu button sits top-right.
references.type: Switzer only. Headlines weight 600, tracking -0.04em, sentence case, charcoal rather than black; statements at 60px, body 13.5px, meta labels about 11px grey. The digest records one element at 15.6vw. Roughly four sizes, one family, no caps.
references.colour: #f1eee9 #e7e2dc #cdc0b0 #3c3c3c #b4a5db #f2e05a — The interface is three close warm beiges with charcoal type; saturated colour (lilac, yellow, olive, terracotta, sand) exists only in photo backdrops and the products themselves.
references.imagery: Studio shots of people interacting oddly with chairs on seamless single-colour backdrops, portrait 3:4, square corners; plus very large cut-out product shots on beige with a soft radial glow and contact shadow, cropped by the panel edge.
references.layout: Outer margins of 16-30px. Sections alternate between split halves, centred statements and left-aligned headings over card rows. Cards are flat rectangles one tone darker than the page with 8px gaps, content pinned to the top-left and bottom edges. Wide empty bands separate sections.

sections.description: A centred four-line statement at about 60px bold with tiny square photo thumbnails, roughly one cap-height tall, dropped inline between words like emoji. Directly beneath, the page splits into two full-width flat colour halves (light greige and tan), each with a small circled plus button in its top inner corner; these are the tops of the two product panels.

Two side-by-side panels in different beiges, each dominated by one enormous cut-out chair (one yellow, one black) cropped at the top so mostly seat and legs show, with a soft radial highlight behind. Along the bottom of each panel: a tiny label and price at left, a row of colour-swatch dots, then two small rectangular buttons at right, one white and one charcoal.

Three equal flat tiles in a row with 8px gaps, each about 210px tall. One short claim is centred in each at roughly 18px, and an index number sits alone in the bottom-left corner in 11px. A small bulleted label hangs above each tile. After a large empty gap, another centred bold statement begins.

A horizontal strip of colour-backdrop photos bleeds off both edges at the top of the section. Below, a left-aligned bold heading at about 40px, then a row of beige cards overflowing to the right: each has an @name at top-left, a short paragraph in 11px, and a bottom row with star glyphs left and a small text link right.

steal: Split the hero 50/50 by background tone alone, park the headline top-left and one tagline bottom-left, and fill the other half with a staggered photo mosaic that leaves grid cells empty.
Keep the interface in three close beige tones and confine all saturated colour to photo backdrops and products, so the photography becomes the palette.
Drop cap-height photo thumbnails inline between the words of a large centred statement.
references.media: A stepped mosaic of seven 175x231 studio photographs (people doing odd things with a chair against one saturated backdrop each) covers about 22% of the fold on the darker right half, bleeding off the right edge; the left half is type. Below come photo chips between the words of a statement, two product halves each with a live 3D chair on its own tone, an auto-scrolling row of portrait tiles, a pinned card deck, and a sticky 3D chair card beside an accordion; square corners everywhere, no video.
references.motion: About 1s of entrance with no preloader: headline lines rise through masks while the mosaic tiles arrive one by one. Lenis holds sticky product halves and pins a story deck for +=400% (3600px), each step bringing the next card in from the right and compressing earlier ones into slivers, and the footer is uncovered by a scrubbed mask over a 728px runway as its slogan letters rise over 1.04s at a 0.04s stagger; micro-interactions are GSAP nudges of 0.2-0.4s on custom eases, and the 3D chairs turn on drag.

references.name: Smallbits
references.idea: The icon set is the page: a full-viewport wall of the product with one docked card holding every word.
references.hero: The whole viewport is a black field tiled with white pixel icons, each drawn about 50px on a 112px pitch, nine rows deep; alternate rows shift half a cell so it reads as a brick pattern, and icons at the edges are cropped. There is no header. A white square-cornered card, 795×170px, is docked bottom-centre: a two-line 24px semibold sentence left, a black rectangular button right, a row of five grey links below. A third-party badge floats top-right. This single screen is the entire page.
references.type: Inter 600 at 24px, -0.02em, for the one sentence; Inter 16px semibold grey for links and button. Nothing exceeds 1.7vw — the pixel icons, not type, are the display element.
references.colour: #000000 #ffffff #9a9a9a #ff6154 — Strict black and white: white icons on black, black text on a white card, grey for secondary links. The only colour is the coral third-party badge.
references.imagery: About ninety visible pixel icons, each an 8×8 bitmap drawn at 50px in pure white with hard edges, tiled full-bleed and cropped at the viewport edges.
references.layout: One viewport, no scroll. A staggered icon grid fills the frame edge to edge; all words live in one docked card. On mobile the card becomes a full-width white block with a full-width button.

sections.description: Mobile restack, the only other state. The icon wall drops to five columns filling the top 73% of the screen; the card becomes a full-width white block at the bottom with the sentence on three lines at 18px, a full-width black button 78px tall, and five grey links spaced evenly on one line.

steal: Make the product the wallpaper: tile the full viewport with the assets at large size and skip a hero image entirely.
Offset alternate rows by half a cell so a regular grid reads as a pattern rather than a table.
Compress all copy, the CTA and the footer links into one docked card so the page never needs to scroll.

references.name: Transport
references.idea: Present a USB stick as a luxury object: one studio render on charcoal above a chrome custom wordmark, then let moody macro photography carry the rest.
references.hero: Flat charcoal field. Centred slightly above the midline, a cut-out render of the drive about 31% of viewport width with its steel arm swung up at 30 degrees. Under it a chrome, ultra-wide custom wordmark spans 72% of the width on one line yet is only 45px tall. Then a centred serif tagline at 2.6vw and a single row: mono spec, a dark pill showing price and sold-out state, mono spec. Logo top-left, a grey centred nav prompt, a small pill with a glowing dot top-right. Carousel chevrons sit at the far left and right edges at product height. The bottom fifth is empty.
references.type: Three voices: a chrome extended techno wordmark as image; Untitled Serif 400 at 38px with -0.026em tracking for taglines and body; ISO mono for specs and caps eyebrows. Section heads switch to a tight heavy Untitled Sans near 36px. Nothing exceeds 3.6vw.
references.colour: #1c1c1c #c8c5ba #6e6f6a #5b5d45 #f1f1ef #2d2d2d — Charcoal base with white text; colour comes only from photographs in grey-olive, concrete and amber. One section flips to dark text over a pale blurred photo.
references.imagery: One clean product render, then shallow-focus macro photographs of the translucent drive on cutting mats, concrete and fabric, graded olive-grey with grain. Full-bleed bands with feathered edges, plus a row of rounded cards of unequal widths.
references.layout: Centred hero, then full-bleed photo bands each carrying one short text group placed differently: top-left, centre-right over a card, bottom-left, centred. Band edges dissolve through heavy blur instead of hard cuts. About 160 words across eleven screens.

sections.description: Full-bleed pale out-of-focus photograph with the drive in sharp focus in the lower half. Dark text overlays the top: a heavy tight grotesk heading at about 36px, left-aligned 8% in from the edge, then three equal columns, each a tiny glyph plus mono caps label over two lines of serif copy. No cards or dividers; the photo's soft blur is the only background.

A full-width macro photo band fades out through a blurred lower edge. On charcoal beneath it, one row of four rounded-corner image cards of unequal widths (one double-width, three single) with narrow gaps, each a tightly cropped lifestyle shot in a different colour temperature. The row is cut by the viewport bottom; further down one card grows taller and pins beside a short text group.

Dark band over a concrete-wall photograph. The drive render floats at top centre, half out of frame, with a horizontal motion streak smeared across the wall behind it. Text sits bottom-left: mono caps eyebrow, heavy grotesk heading, two lines of serif. The band cross-dissolves into an olive bokeh photo holding a centred mono equation, heading and one serif line whose quantities are joined by italic conjunctions.

Two small white script-lettered badges side by side at top centre, like garment labels, with a tiny pill link beneath, then a mostly empty charcoal field. Bottom-left, three tiny stacked mono link groups; bottom-right, white card-suit icons above a two-line italic mono credit, right-aligned.

steal: Pair one centred product cut-out with a very wide, very short metallic wordmark so the logo reads as an engraved nameplate.
Give three typefaces strict jobs: serif for sentences, mono for specs and eyebrows, heavy grotesk for section heads.
Blur the top and bottom edges of full-bleed photo bands so sections melt into each other with no hard seams.
